plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, ensuring non-negative profit whenever you win. Bidding below value only risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses. Since this is a one-shot game with independent draws, I will bid exactly my value of $28 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: you pay the second-highest bid if you win, so shading your bid only risks losing profitable auctions without reducing what you pay. With no information suggesting otherwise, and this being a one-shot game, I'll bid exactly my value of $23 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only win when my value exceeds the second-highest bid, guaranteeing non-negative profit) and never miss out on profitable wins. There's no benefit to shading my bid here, unlike first-price auctions. I'll bid my true value of $36.
